6do6v9:198: : Vercel Connect's core innovation is not better secret management (vault), but completely eliminating the need to store tokens. In traditional architectures, the agent holds long-lived provider tokens—even if stored in a vault, once leaked, the attacker gains full-privilege access. Connect shifts authentication from "holding secrets" to "proving identity": the agent holds no secrets at all, and each time it needs access, it proves its identity via OIDC to obtain short-term, task-scoped credentials.
6g1mna:118: : If you're building agents within the Vercel ecosystem, Connect + eve is the best combination—eve handles agent orchestration, Connect handles external service authentication, and AI Gateway handles LLM routing. This layered architecture is more maintainable than a single-platform approach.
90m1iq:170: : Connect is not a standalone product—it is the security layer of the Vercel agent ecosystem (eve framework + AI Gateway + Connect). eve agents obtain external service credentials through Connect and route LLM calls through AI Gateway, forming a complete "agent security runtime". This layered design is more flexible than a single "agent platform".
